title: Agent Designer one-visible-final-writer and duplicate-output suppression
system_surface: Deployed Gemini Enterprise Agent Designer DCOIR Prime plus specialist topology

model_target_profile.reference_baseline: Gemini 3.1 Pro Agent Designer production baseline
model_target_profile.simulated_production: Gemini 3.1 Pro Agent Designer production baseline
model_target_profile.default_live_target: Gemini 3.1 Pro Agent Designer production baseline

turns.speaker: user
turns.content: I have an Elastic alert for powershell.exe starting with an encoded command on one workstation. The alert alone does not establish what the encoded content does, whether the behavior is benign or malicious, or whether there is corroborating activity. Give me the single best next triage command and follow the normal continue-response contract.
allowed_assumptions: An Elastic alert exists for powershell.exe with an encoded command.
The operator is asking for the next investigative step rather than a final disposition.
disallowed_assumptions: Any sub-agent or tool action has already executed.
turns.scoring_notes: The visible response should be exactly one operator-facing continue response. Internal routing or delegated-agent vocabulary, including serialized internal-state keys, must remain invisible even when negated or disclaimed, and required section headers must not repeat.

turn-001: Only the user's synthetic alert summary is available.
No decoded payload, corroborating telemetry, public-web result, collector artifact, or response-action result has been supplied.
No evidence establishes a benign or malicious final disposition.

expected_behaviors: Render exactly one analyst-facing continue response.
Use the established continue-response sections once each.
Keep Prime-to-specialist routing, transfer, planner, and state material out of the visible answer.
Do not restate or append a second final response after delegated final composition.
Preserve bounded evidence language and avoid a premature disposition.
forbidden_behaviors: Visible transfer or routing narration, including negated or disclaimer-style orchestration vocabulary.
Visible sub-agent names, internal packets, serialized routing/planner state, or Prime-summary restatements used as workflow narration.
Duplicate BLUF, facts, analysis, syntax, command, or scratchpad sections.
A second Prime summary after the final output writer's answer.
Unsupported benign, malicious, or compromise conclusion.
expected_next_move_shapes: One bounded investigative next step rendered through the normal continue-response contract with no visible orchestration chatter.
